newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil rebels attack Sri Lankan army, kill 100.
newsitem.headline: Tamil rebels attack Sri Lankan army, kill 100.

text.p: Tamil Tiger guerrillas killed at least 100 Sri Lankan soldiers in a massive counter-attack on army troops advancing towards the northern rebel stronghold of Kilinochchi on Thursday, military officials said.

In a pre-dawn attack on government forces, members of the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) hit the rear of an army column with mortars, one military officer said asking not to be identified.
"We lost at least 100 soldiers in a massive terrorist counter-attack early this morning," he told Reuters.
About 45 of the dead and 70 wounded had been flown to Colombo by Thursday evening, he said without elaborating.

Thursday's pre-dawn attack was the first reported major assault by the rebels since government troops launched a fresh offensive against their Kilinochchi stronghold last Sunday after a lull in the conflict of more than a month.
This raises the army's death toll to more than 170 and the number of wounded to more than 210 in the fresh offensive.
Earlier on Thursday, a Sri Lankan defence ministry official said troops were advancing slowly towards Kilinochchi under a shower of rocket-propelled grenades and mortar rounds.

The military officer said the rebel attack was on one of the two columns of troops pushing from the road junction town of Paranthan, six km (four miles) north of Kilinochchi, approaching the rebel base from different directions.
He said Tigers also suffered heavy casualties in fierce fighting that followed the rear attack but no figures were available.

A ministry statement earlier reported a rebel counter attack on the western flank. "Latest reports indicate that terrorists launched a massive counter-attack during the very early hours of (Thursday)," it said.
"The counter-attack has been repulsed effectively causing very heavy casualties among the terrorists," it added.
It was not possible to make independent checks to verify claims of warring parties as the government has banned journalists from visiting the war zone.

The LTTE, fighting a 13-year war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, said in their daily radio broadcast that they were engaging the troops with "increased fierceness".
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict since it began in 1983.
Government statistics put the Tigers' total casualties at around 530 dead or wounded.
But army sources said radio communications by the LTTE monitored by the military said only 61 guerrillas, including 23 officers, had been killed.
The armed forces have targeted Kilinochchi since the Tigers overran the military's northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of more than 1,000 men.
